facts.report: Justice Hill Offers PPR Depth and Backfield Insurance: Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill has caught at least three passes in five straight games. He set season highs with five catches and 34 receiving yards on seven targets in Monday night's loss to the Los Angeles Chargers. On third-and-eight, he turned a short pass from Jacoby Brissett into a 25-yard gain to the Chargers' 17-yard line. Hill is rostered in 13% of Yahoo leagues and is worth a Week 11 bench spot in 14-team PPR formats. The Carolina Panthers host Baltimore on Sunday and have allowed 29.4 receiving yards per game to running backs, below the league average of 32.9. He also offers insurance for Derrick Henry managers after playing 33 offensive snaps to Henry's 38 on Monday. They were the only Baltimore running backs with carries, and Henry took 10 of their 13 attempts and scored both Ravens touchdowns. Hill's only game with more than six carries this season came in Week 9 against Jacksonville. He ran nine times for 85 yards that night, with 65 coming on his touchdown.

facts.report: Michael Mayer a Waiver-Wire Target Amid Potential Role Expansion: Across 10 games so far in 2026, Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer has recorded 41 catches for 404 yards and a touchdown on 49 targets. While the 25-year-old has already set career-highs in both receptions and receiving yards, his production has been capped while sharing the field with Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers (ankle). However, Bowers suffered an ankle injury during the team's Week 10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks and could now be facing missed time. If Bowers is sidelined, Mayer could emerge as the top short-area target for Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. While fantasy managers should not expect explosive upside from Mayer, he may be a very valuable player in PPR-scoring formats and could be worth a look on the waiver wire heading into Week 11.

facts.report: Elic Ayomanor Drawing Interest After Increased Workload: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Elic Ayomanor caught five passes for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to Jacksonville. He was targeted 10 times, setting season highs in all three categories. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined, Ayomanor played nearly 95% of Tennessee's offensive snaps and led the team in receiving. Wan'Dale Robinson also left Sunday's game with an ankle injury, leaving the Titans potentially short-handed at receiver heading into Week 11 against Dallas. Ayomanor saw just five targets in his previous game against Cincinnati, so Sunday's workload was a big jump. He's worth a look in 12-team leagues and deeper, particularly if Tate or Robinson misses additional time.
